label: Role (Server RBAC model term)
type: the abstract 'role' entity as defined in Server's own RBAC glossary - 'An entity associated with a fixed set of privileges'. A TBox/model-level term, NOT an instance: do not use it where a specific role belongs (role:full-administrator, role:query-select). Distinct from rbac-role:role, the coarse data-plane placeholder GRANT/REVOKE manipulate, and from capella-role:*, sgw:role and capella:cluster-manager's role sense.
evidence: Role: An entity associated with a fixed set of privileges.
note: The glossary term, promoted so the abstract model has somewhere to live that is not the concrete catalogue. Round 12's headline finding is precisely that these two layers disagree: authorization-overview.md defines role and privilege as separate tiers, and roles.md - the catalogue - documents 56 roles whose permission tables never name a privilege. Keeping rbac-model:role separate from role:* is what lets the registry state that mismatch instead of silently picking a side, which is what round 10 did.
